intro: Shorter notes: what I am tinkering with, what I saw, what I figured out (or did not). Unlike the long posts, these do not aim to be complete.

items.title: Added a table of contents to posts
items.body:
Long posts are hard to read without an outline. From the `lg` breakpoint there is now a sticky table of contents on the right, highlighting the current section as you scroll; on phones it collapses into an expandable "On this page" block.

Heading anchors come from the heading text, and the outline and the body share the same slug rule, so a link cannot point at a section that does not exist.

items.title: Why the blog became a personal archive instead of a post list
items.body:
A post list works well for a site with a lot of content. For a personal site, the first screen should answer "who is this person, and what are they doing?" So the homepage became an introduction, a résumé, and recent writing, while the full archive moved to /posts.

That change also made me realize navigation should not stuff every page into the header. The header now holds four main entries; everything else lives in the footer and in section-level navigation.
